dataset_name: National Inventory of Dams (NID)

Check back in approx. 5 minutes for a new export report' -- i.e. a genuine, working, unauthenticated national bulk-export mechanism, not a dead or gated one.

dataset_name: No single federal bulk file of all API-numbered wells; state oil & gas commission well databases hold the full universe. USGS's Documented Unplugged Orphaned Oil and Gas Well Dataset is a partial federal aggregation (orphaned wells only); BOEM Well Data covers federal offshore wells.
evidence: "United States Documented Unplugged Orphaned Oil and Gas Well Dataset" — "117,672 orphaned wells across 27 states" — "Includes American Petroleum Institute (API) number, or other identification number"
fragmented_exemplars: Texas Railroad Commission (RRC) well records; North Dakota Oil and Gas Division (NDIC) GIS well data; Pennsylvania DEP oil & gas well database
row_count_note: 117,672 orphaned wells across 27 states — but this covers only the orphaned-well subset, not all API-numbered wells.
trap_note: This USGS dataset is a subset (unplugged orphaned wells only), not a national well registry. The authoritative universe of API numbers is fragmented across ~30+ state oil & gas regulatory agencies with no unified federal bulk file.
critic_note: Confirmed and strengthened. Landing page doesn't hold the files itself but its 'View Data Release' link resolves (via DOI 10.5066/P91PJETI) to ScienceBase item 62ebd67bd34eacf539724c56. Queried ScienceBase's JSON API directly and got real file records with working direct-download URIs: US_orphaned_wells.csv (22,186,424 bytes, text/csv) and US_orphaned_wells.zip (8,938,410 bytes), no login required. 117,672-well / 27-state figure and API-number field both confirmed in the item metadata. First pass's honest framing (partial federal aggregation, orphaned wells only, not the full national API-number universe) also checks out -- it's not overclaiming shape.

dataset_name: USGS National Water Information System (NWIS) / Water Data for the Nation
evidence: "Water Data for the Nation" — "Over 135 years of water data from more than one million monitoring locations"
row_count_note: "more than one million monitoring locations"
critic_note: Access shape mislabeled, not a bulk-file dump. waterdata.usgs.gov/nwis redirects (301) to the USGS water-data homepage, which now funnels everything to 'Water Data APIs... REST APIs.' The legacy static bulk-query tool is retired: nwis.waterdata.usgs.gov/nwis/inventory now 302-redirects to a USGS blog post titled 'wdfn-centralized-water-data' explaining the consolidation. I called the live API directly -- https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/site/?format=rdb&stateCd=va&siteType=ST&siteStatus=all -- got HTTP 200 with real tab-delimited site data including the 'site_no' field, no key/login needed. So auth:none holds, but this is api-open, not bulk-file.

dataset_name: USCG Port State Information Exchange (PSIX) Vessel Documentation Search
evidence: "PSIX VESSEL SEARCH" — searchable by "vessel name, Primary Vessel Number, Hull Identification Number (HIN), call sign, flag country, service type, and build year"
trap_note: No bulk-download file found — record-by-record search only, labeled "Primary Vessel Number" rather than "Official Number" though it is the same identifier. Owner PII (name/address) has been stripped from public records since 2018 per earlier search results.
critic_note: Confirmed. PSIX search page has no login wall. Also checked the linked 'PSIX XLSX Export' tool (cgmix.uscg.mil/xml/PSIXExportSearch.aspx, loads with no auth) -- it's a search-parameter-driven export ('Please utilize the search fields below to identify the records you seek'), not a single full-database dump, which matches 'scrape-only' better than it would 'bulk-file.' Claim as stated (scrape-only, no auth) holds.

dataset_name: EPA Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) Basic Data Files
evidence: "TRI Basic Data Files: Calendar Years 1987-Present" — "Each 'Basic' data file contains the 100 most-used data fields from the TRI Reporting Form R and Form A" — "The files are presented in .csv (comma-separated value) format."
trap_note: "Basic" files carry only the 100 most-used fields, not the full Form R/A record — full detail requires a separate download.
critic_note: Confirmed. Page states files are '.csv' format covering the 100 most-used Form R/Form A fields, selectable by year (1987-present) and geography. The visible 'Download data file' href is a javascript:void(0) placeholder that populates dynamically from the year/state dropdowns rather than a static link -- normal for this kind of parameterized government bulk-download tool, not a sign of a broken or gated download. No login encountered.

dataset_name: EPA Superfund Enterprise Management System (SEMS) site data — successor to CERCLIS
evidence: "Superfund Data and Reports" — "Displays site and location information at active sites in SEMS" — legacy "CERCLIS...downloadable files in dBASEIII+ and ASCII text formats representing program data through fiscal year 2013"
trap_note: Legacy CERCLIS archive files are in dBASEIII+/ASCII text format (pre-2014); CERCLIS itself was decommissioned in 2014 and folded into SEMS — old CERCLIS site IDs and current SEMS IDs need to be reconciled, not assumed identical schema.
critic_note: Confirmed. Current SEMS 'Active Site Inventory' and 'Archived Site Inventory' lists are downloadable, and the legacy CERCLIS archive is explicitly available as bulk files: 'CERCLIS dBASEIII+ Format (.dbf)' (55 files) and 'CERCLIS ASCII Text Format (.txt)' (55 files) covering data through FY2013. No authentication barrier found.

id_name: EPA GHGRP Facility ID (Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program)
dataset_name: EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) Data Sets
evidence: "Data Sets | US EPA" — "2023 Data Summary Spreadsheets (zip)" containing "high-level information for facilities"; interactive tools "Envirofacts and FLIGHT" also provide searchable/downloadable access across 32 industry categories
critic_note: Confirmed. Page lists multiple bulk files with no login: '2023 Data Summary Spreadsheets (zip)', 'Emissions by Unit and Fuel Type (zip)', 'Reported Parent Companies (xlsb)', plus several Subpart-specific xlsx files, and also points to Envirofacts for searchable/downloadable access. Matches claim.

id_name: EPA CAMD/CAMPD ORISPL Facility ID + Unit ID
dataset_name: EPA Clean Air Markets Program Data (CAMPD) — facility & unit attributes (ORISPL Facility ID + Unit ID)
evidence: "Clean Air Markets Program Data (CAMPD)" (page title loaded); companion power-sector page references the "EPA-EIA Power Sector Data Crosswalk" whose "methodology to match the different unit IDs is available in R script"
critic_note: Holds, with a real nuance flagged for the record. campd.epa.gov is a JS SPA (WebFetch only sees the static shell/meta tags), so I could not visually confirm the download form. Instead verified at the HTTP/asset level: the URL itself returns 200 with no redirect to a login page; its CSP only whitelists connections to api.epa.gov (self); and I downloaded the main JS bundle (2.96MB) and grepped it -- zero hits for 'sign in', 'login', or 'create account', only 8 generic '401'/'Unauthorized' strings (standard HTTP-error-handling code, not evidence of a login wall on this tool). Separately, EPA's CAM API portal page (epa.gov/airmarkets/cam-api-portal) confirms the *programmatic* CAM API does require a free 'Request API Key' signup -- but that's a distinct product from the web UI at the cited custom-data-download URL, which by all evidence gathered does not require login to use. Net: bulk-file/no-auth claim for this specific URL stands, but flag that automated/API pulls of the same data go through a free-key-gated endpoint.

dataset_name: National Response Center (NRC) spills and incident reports database
evidence: (via fedcenter.gov summary page for NRC) "the sole federal point of contact for reporting oil and chemical spills" — "download Excel files of reports that have been made to the Center"
trap_note: An earlier watchdog report noted the NRC database has been "Down for Maintenance"; rtknet.org is cited as an alternate mirror carrying the same spills/accidents data.
critic_note: Confirmed directly on the cited nrc.uscg.mil URL itself (first pass had actually sourced its quote from a third-party fedcenter.gov page, not the URL under review, but the primary page substantiates it independently): page hosts downloadable Excel spreadsheets of incident reports organized by year (1990-2029) and by decade, with a data dictionary, no login encountered.

dataset_name: EPA Pesticide Product and Label System (PPLS)
evidence: "The Pesticide Product and Label System (PPLS) provides a collection of pesticide product labels...accepted by EPA under Section 3 of the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA)" — searchable "by EPA Registration Number, product name, company name, active ingredients"
critic_note: Confirmed. PPLS is a query form ('enter the information requested below and select the Search button'), searchable by EPA Registration Number, product name, company, active ingredient. No bulk download offered on this page -- matches the claimed scrape-only/no-auth shape.

dataset_name: National List of Active EPA-Registered Foreign and Domestic Pesticide and/or Device-Producing Establishments
evidence: "National List of Active EPA-Registered Foreign and Domestic Pesticide and/or Device-Producing Establishments" — "EPA assigns a unique number to each establishment that produces any pesticide"; exportable as spreadsheet, PDF, or image

dataset_name: USGS/NRCS Watershed Boundary Dataset (WBD)

National 12-digit HUC coverage confirmed.

dataset_name: NRC materials license records — License Verification System (LVS) / Web-Based Licensing, plus Agreement State licensing systems
evidence: nrc.gov pages returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on WebFetch (blocked automated access), so no page content could be directly quoted. Based on WebSearch summaries describing NRC's "License Verification System (LVS)" (deployed 2013) and ADAMS search by license/docket number, and a cited figure of "more than 18,000 source, byproduct, and special nuclear materials licenses" nationally.

id_name: EPA Lead-Safe Certified Firm / Renovator Number
dataset_name: EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting (RRP) Program — Lead-Safe Certified Firm records
evidence: "Renovation, Repair and Painting Program: Firm Certification" — "All applications, payments, updates and certificate replacement requests are done online"; page references a separate firm-search tool
trap_note: The actual firm-search tool (cdxapps.epa.gov/ocspp-oppt-lead/firm-location-search, redirecting to cdxocsppapps.epa.gov) returned 403 Forbidden on WebFetch — only the informational certification page could be loaded directly.
critic_note: Holds, but the cited URL itself doesn't show it -- had to trace one hop further. The renovation-repair-and-painting-program-firm-certification page is actually about firms *applying* for certification, not a public firm-search tool; there's no on-page evidence of a searchable firm database. However, that page does link out to a real 'firm-search' tool at https://cdxocsppapps.epa.gov/ocspp-oppt-lead/firm-search, which I confirmed is live (HTTP 200, no redirect to a login page, no auth wall hit at the HTTP level) -- it's another JS SPA so I couldn't render the actual query form, but nothing indicates a login requirement. Net: a public firm-search tool does exist and appears to need no auth, consistent with the claimed scrape-only/none shape, though the first pass's quoted evidence ('page references a separate firm-search tool') slightly overstates what's literally on the cited page.

id_name: FEMA National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) Community ID Number
dataset_name: FEMA NFIP Community Status Book dataset
evidence: "information on the participation status of a jurisdiction with land use authority, along with attribution of Community Rating System (CRS) status, risk map effective dates" — Dataset ID: FEMA-0137, accessible via the OpenFEMA API
update_cadence_note: "Last Updated: July 1, 2025" (per catalog.data.gov listing loaded)
critic_note: Holds despite a bot block on the human-facing page. www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/... returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch (site appears to bot-filter fetch tools), so I hit the underlying OpenFEMA API directly instead: https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v1/NfipCommunityStatusBook?$top=1 returned real JSON with no login, e.g. communityIdNumber 220169 / GRAND COTEAU, TOWN OF / LA. Confirms the dataset is live, public, and unauthenticated even though the landing page itself is unfriendly to automated fetches.

id_name: EPA UIC Permit ID (Underground Injection Control)
dataset_name: EPA Underground Injection Control (UIC) Program permits — published as individual per-permit web pages; UIC Data Application (uicdata.epa.gov) for state/regional reporting
evidence: "UIC Permit: VAS3G931BSMY" — individual Class III solution-mining permit record for "USC Saltville Brine, LLC" in Saltville, Virginia, which "operates 11 injection wells"
fragmented_exemplars: Railroad Commission of Texas Class II UIC well records; Oklahoma Corporation Commission UIC permits; California Geologic Energy Management (CalGEM) UIC records
trap_note: UIC primacy is state-by-state (most Class II oil/gas injection wells are regulated by state oil & gas agencies, not EPA); EPA's own permit pages are per-permit HTML records, and ECHO's bulk downloads catalog (echo.epa.gov/tools/data-downloads) does not list a standalone UIC bulk dataset.
critic_note: Confirmed exactly as claimed. Page is a single per-permit record (VAS3G931BSMY / USC Saltville Brine, LLC, Saltville VA) with its own annual monitoring reports listed, and no links to a bulk download of all UIC permits -- genuinely scrape-only, one URL per permit, no auth.

id_name: BLM Serial Number (LR2000 / MLRS Case Number)
dataset_name: BLM Mineral & Land Records System (MLRS), successor to LR2000
evidence: "Your existing serial numbers will not become obsolete with MLRS. All serial numbers in LR2000 and ALIS will be transferred to MLRS." — "MLRS will also generate a new standardized serial number for all existing and future cases in MLRS. Both serial numbers are searchable within the system."
critic_note: Claim (api-open, no auth) does not hold up. The cited page's own text ties data access to logging in: 'Once logged in, you can bookmark areas of interest, find public data, and search for locations...' and repeatedly directs users to 'create an MLRS account' to work with cases/serial numbers. No API, no open/anonymous record-lookup path, and no open-data/bulk-download mention anywhere on the page. mlrs.blm.gov itself resolves to a Salesforce Experience Cloud portal (mlrs.blm.gov/s/), consistent with an account-gated system, not an open API. This is an account-required web portal, not api-open/none.

dataset_name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS)
evidence: "Download GNIS Data" — formats: "Pipe-delimited text (TXT) files," "GIS file geodatabase (GDB)," "GeoPackage (GPKG)"
update_cadence_note: "Data products are refreshed bimonthly"
critic_note: Confirmed. Page states downloadable formats include pipe-delimited TXT, file geodatabase (GDB), and GeoPackage (GPKG), served via 'The National Map Staged Products Directory' -- the same public S3-backed bulk mechanism used for other USGS National Map products, no login.

dataset_name: USACE Regulatory Program permit records (ORM2 case-management system), published via per-District public notices — no confirmed single national public bulk file
evidence: permits.ops.usace.army.mil returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on WebFetch, and a secondary usace.army.mil regulatory page rendered only the header "USACE Regulatory" with no body text — no quotable content was directly loaded. Based on general knowledge that USACE Section 404 permitting is administered by ~38 separate District offices, each publishing its own public notices, with ORM2 as the internal case-management system.
fragmented_exemplars: USACE Norfolk District regulatory public notices; USACE Galveston District regulatory public notices; USACE Seattle District regulatory public notices
trap_note: No unified national bulk-download file was confirmed; permit records appear fragmented by USACE District (~38 districts), each with its own public-notice postings and access points.

dataset_name: Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS)
evidence: "authoritative taxonomic information on plants, animals, fungi, and microbes of North America and the world" — "Get ITIS Data" section featuring "Full Database Download" plus "ITIS Solr Web Services"
critic_note: Confirmed and strengthened. Homepage's 'Get ITIS Data' section is real; followed through to itis.gov/downloads/index.html and found live, working download links with no login: itisInformix.tar.gz, itisMSSql.zip, itisMySQLBulk.zip, itisMySQLTables.tar.gz, itisPostgreSql.zip, itisSqlite.zip -- a genuine full-database download in multiple DB formats, plus Solr web services as claimed.

id_name: Legacy EPA AIRS/AFS Facility ID and PCS (Permit Compliance System) ID
dataset_name: EPA ICIS-Air (successor to AFS/AIRS) and ICIS-NPDES (successor to PCS) bulk downloads via ECHO
evidence: "ICIS-Air Dataset (ZIP)" — "Data from EPA's Integrated Compliance Information System (ICIS) for Clean Air Act Stationary Sources" which "replaces the legacy Air Facility System (AFS), which is available as frozen historical data" — "ICIS-NPDES National Dataset (Part 1)" and "Part 2 - effluent violations"
trap_note: Legacy AFS/AIRS Facility IDs are only available as a frozen historical file, not live; ICIS-NPDES (carrying forward legacy PCS permit IDs) is split across Part 1/Part 2 files, which can silently break a join between permits and violations if only one part is pulled.
critic_note: Confirmed. Verified both files directly with curl: https://echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/ICIS-AIR_downloads.zip and https://echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/npdes_downloads.zip both return HTTP 200 with no auth headers/challenges. Page text correctly frames ICIS-Air as the successor to legacy AFS and ICIS-NPDES as successor to legacy PCS.

id_name: USDA NRCS/FSA Conservation Program Contract / Tract Number
dataset_name: No confirmed public bulk dataset at the individual contract/tract level; USDA farm/tract-level conservation program data is generally protected from public release under 7 U.S.C. 1619. EWG's Farm Subsidy Database (built from FOIA'd USDA payment data) is the closest public aggregator, but largely at recipient/program-payment level rather than raw contract/tract-ID granularity.
evidence: Both farm.ewg.org and the FSA CRP program page returned errors on WebFetch (403 and 404 respectively), so no page content could be directly quoted. Based on general knowledge that 7 U.S.C. 1619 restricts USDA release of geospatial/tract-level farm program data, and that EWG's Farm Subsidy Database is built from FOIA requests rather than a native USDA public bulk file.
trap_note: Individual tract-level conservation contract data is protected from disclosure under 7 U.S.C. 1619; the closest public data (e.g., EWG Farm Subsidy Database) is FOIA-derived and typically aggregated to recipient/program level, not raw contract/tract IDs.

dataset_name: OCC Financial Institution Lists (National Banks, Federal Savings Associations & Trust Banks, by charter number)
evidence: The OCC provides downloadable lists in multiple formats for three categories of institutions ... Each category is available sorted by bank name or by state and city, in both Excel and PDF formats (active as of 06/30/2026).
trap_note: Lists are point-in-time snapshot files (Excel/PDF), not a versioned historical archive on this page; the PDF variant lists CHARTER NO / NAME / CERT / RSSD side by side per search-indexed title.
critic_note: Loaded live. Page offers three categories (National Banks & Federal Branches/Agencies, Trust Banks, Federal Savings Associations), each as of 06/30/2026, each downloadable in both Excel and PDF, no login. Quoted evidence matches. One nuance: lists are sorted by bank name or by state/city, NOT literally sorted 'by charter number' as the dataset_name parenthetical implies -- charter number is presumably a column in the file but that wasn't independently confirmed. Core bulk-file/no-auth claim holds.

dataset_name: NCUA Credit Union and Corporate Call Report Data (quarterly, includes charter number)
evidence: This spreadsheet lists all active federally insured credit unions as of the end of the most recent quarter and includes essential metrics, including membership, assets, and loans.
update_cadence_note: quarterly ("as of the end of the most recent quarter")
critic_note: Loaded live. Direct ZIP/spreadsheet link (dated March 2026) with no login, plus a separate Quarterly Data section of comma-delimited files back to March 1994. Quoted evidence matches page text verbatim.

dataset_name: Active Ginnie Mae Issuers (Approved Issuers Directory)
evidence: Issuer name, address, and contact information for Ginnie Mae's active Issuers
trap_note: Ginnie Mae also separately releases an 'issuer file' monthly per its own issuer_tools page copy seen in search indexing (issuer numbers + names), distinct from this data.gov contact-info dataset -- worth reconciling the two before ingest.

Downgrading to 'none-found' for this URL specifically -- the underlying JRFC data may still exist as a real bulk-file/login dataset elsewhere, but that was not established by the cited page and needs fresh research at ojjdp.ojp.gov or NACJD, not just re-verification of this URL.

critic_note: deportationdata.org/data/ice.html loads (200 via curl with a normal browser UA -- WebFetch itself got a 403, which looks like bot-detection on Claude's fetch service, not a real login wall, since a plain browser UA got through fine). Pulled the cited preprint PDF (graemeblair.com/papers/ice-data-preprint.pdf, 200, real PDF) and both quotes check out verbatim: '...we remove 1,494 rows (of 1,323,993 total) for which there is a missing unique identifier' and 'Book In Date Time: This field marks the beginning of an individual's time in a particular detention center.' One nuance: the codebook doesn't have a field literally named 'Book-In Number' -- the unique identifier field is called 'Unique Identifier' (anonymized, derived from A-number) and is separate from the 'Book In Date Time' field. The concept exists and is bulk-downloadable, just not under that exact field name.

More importantly, the quoted evidence is real (confirmed verbatim) but it lives on a completely different page -- ffiec.cfpb.gov/documentation/tools/check-digit -- not the data-browser URL cited in the row. That check-digit page is a one-off calculator/validator (you type in an LEI + loan ID to generate a check digit, or paste a full ULI to validate it); it is not a bulk-download source and can't be used to pull real ULIs in bulk. Separately, CFPB's own site states public HMDA data 'are modified to protect applicant and borrower privacy,' and CFPB's published Modified-LAR policy is known to replace/mask the true ULI rather than publish it as originally reported. So: FFIEC's HMDA Platform does genuinely offer no-login bulk LAR downloads (well-established, kept as best-guess access_shape/auth), but the specific claim that real, usable ULIs are obtainable that way is unverified by the cited evidence and probably wrong given the masking policy. So for the substantive dataset this row is nominally about, 'no auth' is wrong -- it's approval-gated controlled access. The bare accession-number/metadata layer is closer to scrape-only/browse, and I found no evidence of a single no-auth bulk file listing all accessions.

fragmented_exemplars: Netherlands: KVK Handelsregister (kvk.nl) — extracts/API, mostly paid products; Belgium: CBE/KBO Open Data (kbopub.economie.fgov.be) — free bulk file, paid web services for programmatic use; Norway: Brønnøysund Enhetsregisteret (brreg.no / data.brreg.no) — free API + NLOD-licensed bulk download
trap_note: EU e-Justice Business Registers Interconnection System links national registers for search but is not a bulk aggregator — confirmed page text: "the business registers of all EU countries have been interconnected and become searchable", yet the page itself is search-oriented, not bulk-data focused. Cost/auth model also differs sharply by country (NL leans paid, BE/NO lean free).
critic_note: Mixed bag the first pass flattened into one access_shape/auth pair -- NL (KVK) is the weak link. KVK's bulk/programmatic path is the 'Mutatieservice' API, which is explicitly paid: 'You need a subscription and pay a small fee each time you use the link' -- only a fictitious-data sandbox is free; the 'Extract' product is a single-company lookup, mostly paid too. So KVK is NOT a free bulk-file/free-key source as implied. BE (CBE/KBO) does check out as claimed: free but gated behind a mandatory account signup ('Access to this files is free. We only need certain information to secure the data reception') -- true free-key. NO (Brreg) actually beats the claim: 'It is not necessary to register to use the dataset' -- true no-auth bulk access under NLOD, not free-key. LU was never evidenced at all by the first pass -- no URL, no quote -- so it should not have been bundled into a 'confirmed' row. Net: downgrade the row; only 2 of the 3 evidenced countries hold up as free, and the headline country (NL) doesn't.
